readings.title: The Messenger of Defeat
readings.subtitle: The Death of Eli and the Departure of Glory
readings.text: [1 Samuel 4:12] And a man of Binyamin ran from the battle line the same day, and came to Shiloh with his garments torn and dirt on his head. [13] And when he came, see, Ěli was sitting on a seat by the wayside watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And when the man came into the city and reported it, all the city cried out. [14] And when Ěli heard the noise of the cry, he said, “What is the noise of this tumult?” And the man came quickly and told Ěli. [15] Now Ěli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were standing, and he was unable to see. [16] And the man said to Ěli, “I am he who came from the battle. And I fled today from the battle line.” And he said, “What is the word, my son?” [17] And the messenger answered and said, “Yisra’ĕl has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. And your two sons also, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, are dead, and the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> has been captured.” [18] And it came to be, when he made mention of the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, that he fell off the seat backward by the side of the gate. And his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Yisra’ĕl forty years. [19] And his daughter-in-law, Pineḥas’ wife, was with child, near to be delivered. And when she heard the report that the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth, for her labour pains came upon her. [20] And about the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Do not fear, for you have borne a son.” But she did not answer, nor did she set her heart to it. [21] And she called the boy Ikaḇoḏ, saying, “The esteem has departed from Yisra’ĕl!” because the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was taken and because of her father-in-law and her husband. [22] And she said, “The esteem has departed from Yisra’ĕl, for the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> has been captured.”

readings.title: The Ark in Philistia
readings.subtitle: The Humiliation of Dagon
readings.text: [1 Samuel 5:1] And the Philistines took the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> and brought it from Eḇen Ězer to Ashdod. [2] And the Philistines took the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> and brought it into the house of Daḡon and set it by Daḡon. [3] And the Ashdodites rose early in the morning, and see, Daḡon had fallen on its face to the earth before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. So they took Daḡon and put it in its place again. [4] And they rose early on the next morning, and see, Daḡon had fallen on its face to the ground before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. The head of Daḡon and both the palms of its hands were cut off on the threshold, only the fish part of Daḡon was left to him. [5] That is why the priests of Daḡon, and all who come into Daḡon’s house, do not tread on the threshold of Daḡon in Ashdod to this day. [6] And the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was heavy on the Ashdodites, and <dn>He</dn> ravaged them and struck them with tumours, both Ashdod and its borders. [7] And when the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “Do not let the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl remain with us, for <dn>His</dn> hand is hard on us and on Daḡon our mighty one.” [8] And they sent and gathered all the princes of the Philistines to them, and said, “What do we do with the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl?” And they answered, “Let the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl be brought around to Gath.” And they brought the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl around. [9] And it came to be, after they had brought it around, that the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was on the city with a very great destruction. And <dn>He</dn> struck the men of the city, both small and great, and tumours broke out on them. [10] So they sent the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> to Eqron. And it came to be, as the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Eqron, that the Eqronites cried out, saying, “They have brought the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl to us, to kill us and our people!” [11] And they sent and gathered all the princes of the Philistines, and said, “Send away the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, and let it go back to its own place, so that it does not kill us and our people.” For a deathly panic was throughout all the city – the hand of <dn>Elohim</dn> was very heavy there. [12] And the men who did not die were stricken with the tumours, and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.

readings.title: The Return of the Ark
readings.subtitle: Gold Tumours and Milk Cows
readings.text: [1 Samuel 6:1] And the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was in the field of the Philistines seven months. [2] And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, “What do we do with the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? Let us know with what we should send it to its place.” [3] And they said, “If you send away the ark of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, do not send it empty, but you shall certainly return a guilt offering to <dn>Him</dn>. Then you shall be healed, and it shall be known to you why <dn>His</dn> hand is not removed from you.” [4] And they said, “What is the guilt offering which we return to <dn>Him</dn>?” And they answered, “Five golden tumours and five golden rats, according to the number of the princes of the Philistines, for the same plague was on all of you and on your princes. [5] “And you shall make images of your tumours and images of your rats that ravage the land, and you shall give esteem to the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl. It could be that <dn>He</dn> lightens <dn>His</dn> hand from you, and from your mighty ones, and from your land. [6] “And why do you harden your hearts as the Mitsrites and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When <dn>He</dn> had accomplished <dn>His</dn> deeds among them, did they not send them away, and they went? [7] “And now, make a new wagon, and take two milk cows which have never been yoked, and hitch the cows to the wagon. And take their calves home, away from them. [8] “And take the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and put it on the wagon, and put the articles of gold which you return to <dn>Him</dn> as a guilt offering in a chest by its side. And send it away, and it shall go. [9] “And watch: if it goes up the way to its own border, to Bĕyth Shemesh, then <dn>He</dn> has done us this great evil. But if not, then we shall know that it is not <dn>His</dn> hand that struck us – it was an accident that happened to us.” [10] And the men did so, and took two milk cows and hitched them to the wagon, and shut up their calves at home. [11] And they put the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the wagon, and the chest with the gold rats and the images of their tumours. [12] And the cows went straight for the way to Bĕyth Shemesh, going on the one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn aside to the right or the left. And the princes of the Philistines went after them to the border of Bĕyth Shemesh. [13] And those of Bĕyth Shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley. And they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it. [14] And the wagon came into the field of Yehoshua of Bĕyth Shemesh, and stood there, and a great stone was there. And they split the wood of the wagon and offered the cows as a burnt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] And the Lĕwites took down the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the chest that was with it, in which were the articles of gold, and put them on the great stone. And the men of Bĕyth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and made slaughterings the same day to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [16] And when the five princes of the Philistines saw it, they returned to Eqron the same day. [17] And these are the golden tumours which the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: for Ashdod one, for Azzah one, for Ashqelon one, for Gath one, for Eqron one; [18] and the golden rats, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five princes, both walled cities and open villages, as far as the great stone of Aḇĕl on which they set the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – to this day in the field of Yehoshua of Bĕyth Shemesh.

readings.title: A Deadly Inspection
readings.subtitle: The Ark Moved to Qiryath Yearim
readings.text: [1 Samuel 6:19] And <dn>He</dn> struck the men of Bĕyth Shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dn>He</dn> struck fifty thousand and seventy men of the people. And the people mourned because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had struck the people with a great slaughter. [20] And the men of Bĕyth Shemesh said, “Who is able to stand before this set-apart <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn>? And to whom shall <dn>He</dn> go up from us?” [21] And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Qiryath Yearim, saying, “The Philistines have brought back the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Come down, take it up to you.” [1 Samuel 7:1] And the men of Qiryath Yearim came and took the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and brought it into the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ on the hill, and set apart El‛azar his son to guard the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] And it came to be, that from the day the ark dwelt in Qiryath Yearim.

readings.title: Samuel Judges Israel
readings.subtitle: Victory at Mizpah
readings.text: [1 Samuel 7:2b] The time was long, twenty years. And all the house of Yisra’ĕl lamented after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] And Shemu’ĕl spoke to all the house of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “If you return to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with all your heart, then put away the foreign mighty ones and the Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and serve <dn>Him</dn> only, so that <dn>He</dn> delivers you from the hand of the Philistines.” [4] And the children of Yisra’ĕl put away the Ba‛als and the Ashtaroth, and served <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> only. [5] And Shemu’ĕl said, “Gather all Yisra’ĕl to Mitspah, and let me pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for you.” [6] And they were gathered to Mitspah, and drew water and poured it out before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they fasted that day, and said there, “We have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” And Shemu’ĕl judged the children of Yisra’ĕl at Mitspah. [7] And the Philistines heard that the children of Yisra’ĕl had gathered together at Mitspah, and the princes of the Philistines went up against Yisra’ĕl. And when the children of Yisra’ĕl heard of it, they were afraid of the Philistines. [8] And the children of Yisra’ĕl said to Shemu’ĕl, “Do not cease to cry out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> for us, that <dn>He</dn> save us from the hand of the Philistines.” [9] And Shemu’ĕl took a suckling lamb and offered it as an entire burnt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Shemu’ĕl cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for Yisra’ĕl, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered him. [10] And as Shemu’ĕl was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Yisra’ĕl. But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> thundered with a loud thunder upon the Philistines that day, and confused them, and they were smitten before Yisra’ĕl. [11] And the men of Yisra’ĕl went out of Mitspah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them as far as below Bĕyth Kar. [12] And Shemu’ĕl took a stone and set it up between Mitspah and Shĕn, and called its name Eḇen Ězer, saying, “Thus far <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has helped us.” [13] And the Philistines were humbled, and they did not come any more into the border of Yisra’ĕl. And the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was against the Philistines all the days of Shemu’ĕl. [14] And the cities which the Philistines had taken from Yisra’ĕl were restored to Yisra’ĕl, from Eqron to Gath. And Yisra’ĕl delivered its border from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Yisra’ĕl and the Amorites. [15] And Shemu’ĕl judged Yisra’ĕl all the days of his life. [16] And he went from year to year on a circuit to Bĕyth Ěl, and Gilgal, and Mitspah, and judged Yisra’ĕl in all those places. [17] But he always returned to Ramah, for his home was there. And there he judged Yisra’ĕl, and there he built an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: A Request for a King
readings.subtitle: Israel Rejects the Kingship of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [1 Samuel 8:1] And it came to be when Shemu’ĕl was old that he made his sons judges over Yisra’ĕl. [2] And the name of his first-born was Yo’ĕl, and the name of his second, Aḇiyah – judges in Be’ĕrsheḇa. [3] But his sons did not walk in his ways, and turned aside after own gain, and took bribes and twisted right-ruling. [4] And all the elders of Yisra’ĕl gathered together and came to Shemu’ĕl at Ramah, [5] and said to him, “Look, you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint for us a king to judge us like all the nations.” [6] But the word was evil in the eyes of Shemu’ĕl when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.” So Shemu’ĕl prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ĕl, <dq>“Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected <dn>Me</dn> from reigning over them.</dq> [8] <dq>According to all the works which they have done since the day that <dn>I</dn> brought them up out of Mitsrayim, even to this day – forsaking <dn>Me</dn> and serving other mighty ones – so they are doing to you too.</dq> [9] <dq>And now, listen to their voice, only you shall certainly warn them, and make known to them the ruling of the king who does reign over them.”</dq>

readings.title: The Manner of the King
readings.subtitle: The Cost of Earthly Monarchy
readings.text: [1 Samuel 8:10] And Shemu’ĕl spoke all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the people who asked him for a king. [11] And he said, “This is the ruling of the king who reigns over you: He takes your sons and appoints them for his own chariots and to be his horsemen, and some run before his chariots. [12] “And he appoints captains over his thousands and captains over his fifties, and some to plow his ground and reap his harvest, and some to make his weapons of battle and equipment for his chariots. [13] “And he takes your daughters to be perfumers, and cooks, and bakers. [14] “And he takes the best of your fields, and your vineyards, and your olive trees, and gives them to his servants. [15] “And he takes a tenth of your grain and of your vintage, and gives it to his officers and servants. [16] “And he takes your male servants, and your female servants, and your best young men, and your donkeys, and uses them for his own work. [17] “He takes a tenth of your sheep, and you are his servants. [18] “And you shall cry out in that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not going to answer you in that day.” [19] However, the people refused to listen to the voice of Shemu’ĕl, and said, “No, but let a king be over us! [20] “Then we shall be, we also, like all the nations, and our king shall judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.” [21] And Shemu’ĕl heard all the words of the people, and he spoke them in the hearing of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [22] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ĕl, <dq>“Listen to their voice, and make them a king.”</dq> And Shemu’ĕl said to the men of Yisra’ĕl, “Go each of you to his city.”
